records.title: The Founding Conversation
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A conversation about lost context became the ConvoCanvas plan: preserve conversations, organise them in a vault and turn them into useful knowledge. The published episode describes planning here; implementation follows in the next chapter.
records.editorialNote: Chronology correction: this was the planning conversation. Vault implementation and ChromaDB indexing appear in the following September chapters.

records.title: From the vault plan to a working MVP
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: The vault, LibreChat and a first FastAPI backend gave the idea a working path: upload a conversation, parse it and extract content ideas.

records.title: Local models and conversation ownership
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Ollama and local models opened a second path for working with conversations. The episode explores control, model selection and the limits that remained.

records.title: The vault becomes searchable
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: ChromaDB integration turned a growing collection of Markdown into semantic search. The episode follows the implementation and scaling work across the week.

records.title: The migration question
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Research into update speed and operational cost led to a hybrid deployment decision. Existing K3s workloads did not mean every service should move into the cluster.

records.title: Recovering the K3s cluster
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A failing cluster exposed networking and recovery assumptions. The chapter follows diagnosis, recovery and the need for better operational visibility.

records.title: Teaching the platform to draw its architecture
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Generated architecture diagrams made the growing platform easier to inspect and reduced the work of maintaining a separate mental picture.

records.title: The platform starts telling its own story
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: The same vault and search tooling helped reconstruct the first season. Publishing and episode navigation became part of the system being built.

records.title: Temporal Filtering
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Reconstructing the early journal exposed a date problem: archive filenames could obscure when the work actually happened. Temporal search and metadata handling were corrected.

records.title: Validation becomes a development habit
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Code review, systematic checks and metadata debugging tested whether recent improvements behaved as expected. The story makes the verification work visible alongside implementation.

records.title: 54 Minutes to Production
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Capture cleanup, semantic chunking, architecture auditing and publishing tools advanced across several short sessions. The episode distinguishes active work from the elapsed overnight window.

records.title: Testing several systems together
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A vault reindex, Journal v3, hybrid search and developer commands met in one testing window. Feature flags and measured trade-offs mattered as much as getting services deployed.

records.title: Turning research into operating patterns
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Agent patterns, evaluation and resumable work were introduced alongside recovery and learning work. The episode also records the gap between agent-assisted execution and personal understanding.

records.title: From side project to platform
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A long engineering arc brought storage migration, a rebrand and a more structured platform. This is a retrospective covering several months, not a single-day deployment.

records.title: Rebuilding the journal pipeline
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Unreliable generated journals prompted a Kafka-based pipeline, fuller session context and quality checks. The published chapter records iterations and limits rather than treating generated prose as evidence by itself.

records.title: Sealed Secrets + Harbor
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.

records.title: The synthesis layer learns to refuse
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: The Matrix bot checked retrieval relevance before synthesis and refused when the evidence was too weak. The episode dates this engineering to February; the public ADR carries a later record date.

records.title: PDG Activation — Code Intelligence
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.

records.title: The audit and the cascade
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A security investigation became a chain of dependency repairs, rollback, metadata cleanup and documentation work. The published event window is March, separately from the later SRE milestones.

records.title: The weekend search got measurably better
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Benchmark-led fixes exposed scoring defects and a costly search path. The MCP transport migration improved connection behaviour, while deeper retrieval bottlenecks remained.

records.title: Async search and the missing evidence
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: An async retrieval refactor and a path-traversal fix improved different parts of the platform. The account also explains why retained journals had to stand in for missing raw transcripts.

records.title: The fleet, the connectors and the async ceiling
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Fast search gains did not solve deep-search latency. Graph freshness, incomplete consumers and connector design led to a more explicit retrieval and evaluation programme.

records.title: The great restructure and the measurement era
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: The repository became a sixteen-package workspace while CI, memory evaluation and embedding contention were addressed. The chapter closes the season with clearer boundaries and a stronger decision trail.

records.title: The night the fleet audited everything
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: A structured audit found defects across client isolation, Kafka durability, feature flags and graph handling. The work paused and resumed; findings still needed remediation and verification.

records.title: Proving the fixes were real
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Live probes and benchmark reruns checked the audit fixes. Missing raw benchmark outputs and a misleading judge comparison exposed why a result needs replayable evidence.

records.title: Git history for the agent’s context
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Vault and harness configuration gained versioning, recovery checks and clearer provenance. This describes the June custody model; the October operating model is recorded separately.

records.title: Building the cockpit
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Operational noise, ingestion work and metadata repairs made a shared review surface necessary. The first Console combined a review tracker, canvas and visible provenance.

records.title: The cockpit becomes an instrument panel
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
records.description: Live vault views, voice capture, interactive sessions and explicit approvals joined into an idea-to-session-to-review loop. Terminal access in this period was read-only.

records.dateLabel: 11–12 June 2026 · opening of a longer arc
records.title: Giving the Codex lane its own guardrails
records.evidenceLabel: Backfilled through 14 June only. The linked episode also contains later work.
records.description: Separate configuration, valid hook responses and visible usage were the first steps. This milestone covers the opening work only; the published episode continues through 18 June, including the later handoff design.

records.dateLabel: 12 June 2026 · opening of the budget arc
records.title: Choosing an authoritative usage meter
records.evidenceLabel: Backfilled through 14 June only. The linked episode also contains later work.
records.description: Codex’s guard read server-provided rate-limit windows, while the Claude guard still estimated usage from local transcripts. The later recalibration and deduplication work is beyond this 14 June backfill.

records.title: The machine had one memory budget
records.evidenceLabel: Historical account from the published journal. Dates describe engineering, not publication.
